br01.gold_connection: The 41 promo redemptions and the 44 app signups on 3 May came from one scripted batch of postbin.io mailboxes numbered 0408 to 0451, so the two products were hit by the same operator and the store's promo log is a ready-made blocklist for the app.
br01.gold_implication: Join the store's SPRING24 customer emails with the app's 3 May signups on the local part, confirm the overlap, and block the postbin.io four-digit-suffix pattern at both signups.
br01.hidden_mechanism: the numbered postbin.io mailbox batch that redeemed the store promo is the same scripted account batch that signed up on the app

br02.gold_connection: The store's 30-euro low-value authentication exemption enabled on 12 June covers the shared merchant account, which is why the app's 29.90 top-ups from new accounts exploded on the same day: attackers price just under the threshold that skips the extra check.
br02.gold_implication: Ask the processor whether the exemption is scoped per merchant account or per storefront, and compare app chargebacks on 29.90 top-ups before and after 12 June.
br02.hidden_mechanism: the 30-euro low-value exemption switched on for the store applies to the whole merchant account, so the app's 29.90 top-ups ride the same exemption

br03.gold_connection: The description generator's 4.6 score was measured on SKUs 1000 to 1199, the merchandiser's hand-picked set, while every generated description in production is for SKUs 1200 and up, the range where "not as described" returns tripled; the score and the returns never overlap.
br03.gold_implication: Re-run the description eval on a random 100 SKUs from 1200 upward and compare the score with the 4.6.
br03.hidden_mechanism: the description generator is evaluated on SKUs 1000 to 1199 and used only on SKUs 1200 and up, so the 4.6 score never touches the products that get returned

br04.gold_connection: The 0.6 drop in the support-reply quality score on 19 August is the eval vendor's judge snapshot change of the same date, which moved reference-set scores by a similar amount; nothing about the store's replies changed.
br04.gold_implication: Re-score last week's replies with the previous judge snapshot pinned and check whether the 0.6 gap disappears.
br04.hidden_mechanism: the vendor dashboard's quality score dropped on 19 August because the vendor swapped its judge snapshot that day, not because the store's reply model changed

br05.gold_connection: The four missed morning doses since August all fall on Tuesdays because the new carrier contract from 2 August moved dispatch to a 06:30 cutoff, and the dose is scheduled at 07:00, inside the packing rush.
br05.gold_implication: Move the dose to 06:00 on Tuesdays for four weeks and check whether the tracker shows any Tuesday miss.
br05.hidden_mechanism: the Tuesday 06:30 dispatch cutoff introduced on 2 August is why every missed morning dose since then falls on a Tuesday

br06.gold_connection: The store's temperature excursions and the cloudy vials share one cause: FrostLine's 14:00 pickup, which is the van whose reefer logs show warm periods; the 09:00 pickup on the same contract has none.
br06.gold_implication: Move both the store's cold-chain shipments and the vial deliveries to the 09:00 FrostLine slot for a month and compare excursion logs and vial condition.
br06.hidden_mechanism: FrostLine's 14:00 pickup runs on the van with the failing reefer, so both the store's cold-chain excursions and the cloudy vials trace to that slot

br07.gold_connection: The grant portal rejects the SME declaration because the VAT number entered is the new one issued on 1 April while the 2025 financial statements it validates against carry the old number; the rejection is an identifier mismatch, not an eligibility problem.
br07.gold_implication: Resubmit the declaration with the old VAT number that appears on the 2025 accounts and attach the change notice, then check whether the validation passes.
br07.hidden_mechanism: the VAT number changed on 1 April, so the grant portal's SME check against the 2025 financials fails on an identifier mismatch, not on eligibility

br08.gold_connection: The warped boards all came from stock staged on shelf C of the workshop overflow, the shelf where the humidity sensor reads 78 percent every night, so the warping is storage, not a supplier defect.
br08.gold_implication: Move the remaining board stock off shelf C, keep the sensor there, and check whether the next 30 board orders produce any warping return.
br08.hidden_mechanism: shelf C in the workshop overflow reads 78 percent humidity every night, and every warped board returned came from stock held on shelf C

br10.gold_connection: The consortium deliverable "EvalBench Pro score above 70 at month 24" is undefined because EvalBench Pro re-normalised its scale between its 1 June and 1 September snapshots, moving the same unchanged model from 71 to 64; the deliverable must pin a snapshot.
br10.gold_implication: Amend the deliverable to name the 1 June 2026 EvalBench Pro snapshot and re-check the baseline number against that snapshot before submission.
br10.hidden_mechanism: EvalBench Pro re-normalises its scores across snapshots, so a 24-month deliverable defined as an EvalBench Pro score cannot be met or missed on its own terms

br12.gold_connection: The unknown-device login on the grant portal at 03:12 on 22 July and the credential burst on the app at 03:10 the same night came from the same network block, two minutes apart, right after the consortium Slack export with both credentials was shared publicly.

br12.hidden_mechanism: the consortium Slack export leaked on 22 July, and both the portal login attempt and the app's credential-stuffing burst at 03:10 that night came from the same network

br13.gold_connection: The grant interview in Brussels on 6 November at 09:00 falls on the morning of the fasting blood draw booked for 08:00 the same day, which means either a 05:40 flight while fasting or moving one of the two.

br15.gold_connection: The judge latency doubling and the 3 percent error rate between 13:00 and 15:00 since early August come from the eval GPU box sitting in the shed, which the temperature logger shows at 41 degrees in that window since the AC schedule changed on 1 August.

br18.gold_connection: The signup numbers that pass SMS verification but never answer a call belong to Telsim's machine-to-machine range 6 22 34 xx, the same range printed on the workshop's sensor SIMs, which are data-only and cannot take a voice call by design.

br19.gold_connection: Deep sleep dropped 35 percent from 20 August, the night the bedroom window was sealed to route the new sensor cable; the CO2 sensor on the same cable shows 1,900 ppm from 02:00 to 06:00 since that night.

br20.gold_connection: Resting heart rate is 6 bpm higher on Tuesday and Friday mornings because the laser cutter runs on Monday and Thursday evenings and the workshop monitor logs PM2.5 spikes to 90 micrograms per cubic metre each time, the evening before each raised morning.

br21.gold_connection: The fraud model's eval passes because its 40 fraud items use the test BIN 411111, the same BIN the production rule whitelists as a test card, so any real card with a 411111 prefix sails through and the eval can never show it.

br21.hidden_mechanism: the eval's fraud items all use test BIN 411111, and the production model whitelists BIN 411111 as a test card, so the eval cannot see the whitelist hole

br22.gold_connection: The gold labels the models keep disagreeing with are the 120 written on 3 to 5 July, the three days the health log shows a 38.5 degree fever and ibuprofen; the labels from the surrounding days have no such disagreement.
